correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a single parent event P_j=v has exactly two effects on leaf indicators born before j: it forces v to be nonleaf and removes the time-j hazard from every other earlier vertex. Later leaf events are independent. Exact summation yields the local covariance and harmonic aggregate formula. Strict discrete convexity proves a single finite sign crossing, and harmonic asymptotics yield the limiting profile and Lambert-W threshold.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources are broader for their respective marginals or profile vectors but do not, in the accessible statements, retain a specified birth label and pair its child count with the global leaf count. The accepted theorem requires this age-resolved mixed statistic.

evidence: A root-degree/leaf relation would not imply the nonroot formula because the root has a structurally forced early child and lacks a leaf event once n is at least two.
Global degree-count covariance collapses birth labels and therefore cannot determine the age-resolved sign transition.
Depth-profile sign changes concern levels rather than deterministic labels and use a different indexing geometry.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The accepted claim depends on how one time-j attachment simultaneously removes one leaf possibility and protects all competing earlier vertices. That mechanism is not recoverable from a marginal degree law, a marginal leaf law, or a covariance matrix after labels have been aggregated.

originality.rationale: The inspected full archive source on recursive-tree high degrees does not discuss leaves, while the classical terminal-vertex source treats the leaf statistic without the displayed labeled-vertex covariance. Published profile-correlation work has sign changes in depth-indexed level counts, and degree-distribution work studies global degree classes, but neither accessible statement gives the local j=2v law or the birth-label threshold.
residual_risks: Older joint recursive-tree literature may contain the same mixed moment under different degree or terminal-vertex notation.
Only abstract-level material was accessible for some classical sources, so whole-document noncoverage is not asserted for them.
The novelty claim is the local attachment sign law and the induced age threshold, not the known marginal leaf distribution or degree-profile asymptotics.

value.rationale: A labeled vertex's child count and the global number of leaves are canonical local and global observables of recursive-tree growth. The theorem isolates an exact competing-effect mechanism at one attachment, derives a complete finite sign classification, and produces a natural macroscopic phase boundary rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
